answer_sql:
SELECT
  COUNT(DISTINCT order_key) AS how_many_orders
FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line

  AND order_date >= CAST('2024-01-01' AS DATE)

sections.title: What it says its rows are

body.value: One figure: how many separate orders were placed in euros between 1 January and 31 March 2024 — 1,099 of them, one per `order_key`. It sits inside the 20,530 euro orders of all time and the 93,470 orders the bundle holds. It counts ORDERS and says nothing about what they were worth: no revenue, no units, no average, and no amount in euros or any other currency. It leaves out every order in USD, GBP, CAD or AUD placed in that same quarter — 4,816 orders were placed in the quarter across all five currencies, so 3,717 are set aside — and every euro order placed outside the quarter. It counts by when an order was PLACED, so a euro order placed 2024-03-29 and delivered in April is in, and one placed in December 2023 and delivered in January 2024 is out; the delivered reading would be 1,121.

  COUNT(
    DISTINCT CASE
      WHEN order_date >= CAST('2024-01-01' AS DATE)
      AND order_date < CAST('2024-04-01' AS DATE)
      THEN order_key
    END
  ) AS eur_orders_by_order_date,
  COUNT(
    DISTINCT CASE
      WHEN delivery_date >= CAST('2024-01-01' AS DATE)
      AND delivery_date < CAST('2024-04-01' AS DATE)
      THEN order_key
    END

  MIN(
    CASE
      WHEN order_date >= CAST('2024-01-01' AS DATE)
      AND order_date < CAST('2024-04-01' AS DATE)
      THEN order_date
    END
  ) AS first_order_date_in_window,
  MAX(
    CASE
      WHEN order_date >= CAST('2024-01-01' AS DATE)
      AND order_date < CAST('2024-04-01' AS DATE)
      THEN order_date
    END
  ) AS last_order_date_in_window,
  COUNT(
    DISTINCT CASE
      WHEN order_date >= CAST('2024-01-01' AS DATE)
      AND order_date < CAST('2024-04-01' AS DATE)
      THEN DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', order_date)
    END
  ) AS months_present_in_window
FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line
WHERE
  currency_code = 'EUR'
